title: epochal-worklet-stitcher-and-queue-contention-replayer
author: Ethan Kline
description: Motivation: We need a deterministic harness that reproduces short-lived queue contention and scheduler jitter seen in production LLM serving clusters. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) an epochal worklet stitcher that composes short-lived microtasks (worklets) into synthetic request trajectories with explicit epochs (warmup, steady, spike, cooldown) and (2) a queue contention replayer that can inject multi-consumer queue lengths, consumer sleep/jitter profiles, and CPU affinity switches to reproduce head-of-line blocking and tail amplification. Design summary: the worklet stitcher is a lightweight DSL (YAML/JSON) for expressing per-epoch distributions (arrival, size, KV cache hit rates, prefix lengths) and inter-epoch transitions. The contention replayer accepts recorded schedule traces (produced by the collector in this PR) and drives a local multi-threaded runner that models queue lengths and backpressure signaling. Both tools can be used independently or together in end-to-end suites. Implementation: new package bench/worklet_stitcher with a small runtime and generator; bench/contention_replayer that includes an efficient lockless queue emulator and a pluggable CPU-affinity shim on Linux (using sched_setaffinity). Added a trace exporter compatible with existing flamegraph pipeline. Usage: examples/recipes/epochal_small.yaml demonstrates a 10-minute run reproducing a production spike pattern. Invocation: benchctl run --recipe examples/recipes/epochal_small.yaml --replayer traces/spike-2025-11-18.json --out reports/epochal-2026-01-12.json. Backwards compatibility: existing workload runners continue to work; the stitcher adds an opt-in recipe format. Testing: unit tests for the stitcher grammar, integration test that compares steady-state latency histograms with a golden trace (CI runs a short mode). Why unique: this targets micro-scheduler level artifacts (queue contention + affinity churn) instead of just request mixing; helps validate runtime preemption and kernel scheduling heuristics.

b4d2c3e: implement lockless queue emulator and CPU affinity shim
c9f7a0d: add recipe examples and documentation
d1e2f3b: add trace exporter and flamegraph compatibility
e6f4b2a: CI integration and smoke tests (short mode)
review_comments: Maya Patel: Nice DSL. Question: can the stitcher express correlated KV cache hit patterns across epochs? (e.g., cache warms then drifts).
Ethan Kline: Yes — recipe supports 'cross_epoch_seed' and an optional 'session_affinity' block. Added example in epochal_small.yaml.
Lucas Morin: affinity shim is Linux-only; add a no-op shim for macOS and Windows to avoid build breaks.
Ethan Kline: added platform stubs and conditional build tags; CI short-mode verifies build on macOS runner.
Priya Suresh: Integration test is flaky in CI (timing-related). Can we reduce reliance on wall-clock exactness?
Ethan Kline: switched to quantile-based assertion (p50/p95 ranges) and added retries in CI short-mode; also instrumented test to use a deterministic RNG seed.
release_notes: Add epochal worklet stitcher and queue contention replayer to benchmark-lab. New recipes and replayer traces enable deterministic reproduction of short-lived queue contention and affinity churn. CI includes a short-mode to run smoke validation.
notes_for_operators: When running long recipes against production-scale traces, use --profile-kernel to capture kernel-level scheduling samples; replayer uses raw sched_setaffinity and requires CAP_SYS_NICE or equivalent in some environments.
changelog_summary: Introduce epochal workload composer and queue contention replayer for deterministic micro-scheduler stress tests.
manual_test_instructions: 1) checkout repo; 2) make build; 3) cp examples/recipes/epochal_small.yaml .; 4) benchctl run --recipe epochal_small.yaml --out /tmp/epochal.json; 5) open reports/epochal-*.json in bench/docs/viewer or run scripts/plot_latency.py
notes_on_future_work: Planned follow-ups: integrate with perf-canary to run targeted epoch recipes in canary clusters, add GPU-aware worklets that exercise host->device transfer stalls, and add a cloud-scale distributed replayer variant.
author_reply_summary: Addressed platform stubs, made integration tests deterministic, added documentation and recipes, and squashed commits per reviewer requests.
